_comment: Mike Schmidt Memorial Iron Team Award placings, from third-party reporting.
The award recognises the TOP THREE teams by cumulative score across the three
North American Baja SAE events in a season — not a single winner. A team that
received it has not necessarily won it.
This file is CORROBORATION ONLY. The podium shown on the site is computed from
SAE's own published results by total points, which is the award's actual
definition. Checking the two against each other validates both: at Baja SAE
2014 the computed top three are Cornell, Michigan and RIT, matching the
Each entry carries an explicit `place` (1, 2, 3, or null where a source records
a placing without saying which) and a `confidence`:
confirmed      independently sourced as that place
reported       a single team-history source states it; not corroborated
place-unknown  the team placed, but the source does not say where
Team history pages enumerate a team’s placings across many years, so a bare
mention on one is not evidence of a win. Recording every such mention as a
first place was an earlier error in this file.
History starts at 2013. Corrections welcome via an issue or pull request.

researchNotes.unknownYearsInvestigated: 2003, 2004, 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2011 were searched extensively across university news, team history pages and SAE articles without finding a winner. They are deliberately left blank rather than inferred.

ruledOut.rit: Won exactly three times — 2001, 2002, 2018 — per two RIT sources, so RIT did not win any of the unknown years.
ruledOut.cornell: Iron Team only in 2014 and 2025; the team was founded in 2003 and first competed in 2005.
ruledOut.michigan-tech: The 2009 win was reported as the first in school history, so Michigan Tech did not win 2003-2008.
